_comment: MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, on BOTH halves — 2026-09-26, browser 1.18.0, on a box with a booking.com login. The marker is data-testid="auth-link-in-view", `5dive reflex login-marker`'s top pick: `5dive browser capture booking.com` matched it once in each of two logged-out renders and 0 times in the logged-in render, where the header shows 'Your account' + Genius level instead, and `status booking.com` read authenticated with this file installed. THE MARKER IS A REGEX (grep -iE here, RegExp in the served browser). The first draft used the link's href as it was counted, account.booking.com/auth/oauth2?client_id= : as a regex `2?` is an optional 2, so it matched 0 of the 2 logged-out captures and would have stamped every logged-out profile authenticated. A plain fetch of the home page is a 202 with an empty body, so the marker cannot be read off curl. SEARCH NEEDS THE SERVED BROWSER: a cold act/run of any searchresults URL (even one copied from a real browser) is redirected to the undated /city/pt/lisbon.html SEO page; the same URL through `serve booking.com` returns the dated results. ss=<city name> is enough, no dest_id needed (477 results for Lisbon 14-15 Oct).

search._comment: Dated search, every property type, under {max_eur} per stay, cheapest first. Run `serve booking.com` first (see the top comment). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. The verify block cannot re-read the results (Booking serves a public curl a different page), so expect NOT VERIFIED and read the result page instead.

hotels._comment: Same as search, restricted to hotels (ht_id=204) rated 8+ (review_score=80). Lisbon 14-15 Oct, 2 adults, max 120: 25 found, cheapest Dom Joao Glamour EUR 95, Avenida Park EUR 98, ibis Alfragide EUR 107.
